rv.q: It has not been a vintage season for the jukebox musical.
This dreary enterprise hits a smirk-inducing note of steamy camp when the climactic 'Hot Feet' ballet finally arrives.

cn.t: Critics are sharply divided on this Earth, Wind & Fire jukebox musical, with reactions ranging from moderate appreciation to harsh dismissal of the show's execution.

sg.ra: In a 1,622-seat house that fits Broadway's deepest orchestra, sitting up close is worth the premium — SeatPlan specifically names seats 1-14 in rows A-E as 'not too close for comfort' with a 'good distance to combine detail with striking views of the whole set.' Cursed Child stages illusions at ground level where facial reactions matter; one BWW poster frequent to the show says even Dress Circle Row C 'feels a bit too far back.' Note: Lyric's orchestra is split down the middle (two sections, not three), so 'center' here is seats 1-2 hugging the centerline.

The value play in a house this big: far enough back that Cursed Child's wide staging and aerial work register as a full picture, close enough that the illusion work still reads. A BWW regular recommends 'Orchestra Row O a few seats in from center aisle' or 'Row L about halfway down'; Tickadoo calls rows H-M 'excellent views at more moderate pricing.' Critically, the Dress Circle overhang starts at row Q, so rows F-P are the last orchestra rows NOT under the mezz lip — meaning full head-height for aerial effects. Seats 1-14 (centerline side) stay squared to the stage; seats past 15 angle toward the side wall.

This is the Lyric's structural weak point: the orchestra runs 27 rows (AA-ZZ) and is 'much deeper than other Broadway theatres' per SeatPlan. The Dress Circle overhang hits at row Q and cuts into the top of the stage by row W — a real problem for Cursed Child, which hides illusion setups upstage in shadow (per Exeunt, lighting designer Neil Austin 'shrouds much of the set in upstage shadow to hide whatever Harrison needs to pull off'). Multiple Tripadvisor reviewers explicitly say 'avoid the part of the orchestra that is overhung by the dress circle.' Tickpick: 'avoid the final rows (R-S); consider Dress Circle seats instead.'

sg.n: Dress Circle Center Front (Rows A-C, seats 107-116)
sg.ra: The only section where Cursed Child's full staging plan works as designed. A Tripadvisor reviewer flags that the production has 'special effects sequences that take advantage of the permanent residency to involve the full scope of the auditorium' — multiple BWW posters say 'there's a scene that can only be properly seen from the dress circle or balcony.' Tickadoo specifically calls Dress Circle 'excellent vantage point for aerial effects.' Headout names seats 107-116 in rows A-C as optimal. Watch-out: SeatPlan notes 'a high safety bar in front of row A may negatively affect views for shorter patrons' — the Tripadvisor reviewer at 5'2" had trouble even with a booster.

Keeps the Dress Circle's key advantage — elevated sightline over the full proscenium for aerial/illusion work Cursed Child was designed to showcase — at a lower price point than rows A-C. Headout and Tickadoo both call rows D-F/E-J 'sweeping view' at moderate pricing. One Tripadvisor reviewer notes the Dress Circle has a 'steeper rake, making the view easier for a small child.' Center section only; SeatPlan warns Dress Circle side sections (seats in the low single digits or high 20s) have 'restricted views into the sides of the stage.'

The one Balcony play worth making for Cursed Child specifically. SeatPlan: 'The best views in the Balcony are from the front rows, A to C. These are very high and somewhat distant from the stage, but usually unobstructed.' Cursed Child was built for this — one Balcony-seated reviewer reports 'Dementors are flying right past you' from front rows; another says 'you get to see all the show and effects (if you have vertigo it may feel a little bit scary).' SeatPlan also flags 'superior legroom' continues up into the Balcony, a Lyric-wide trait noted across every source. Caveat: Tripadvisor reviewer at 5'2" struggled even with booster seats; safety bar is the issue.

sg.n: Balcony Rear & Sides (Rows D-H, all sides)
sg.ra: At this distance in a 1,622-seat house, you're watching a lit postage stamp — Tickpick notes Balcony viewers report 'requires leaning forward to see stage action,' a problem for any show but especially Cursed Child's 5-hour Part One + Part Two runtime. SeatPlan specifically warns the 'far side seats, especially in row A, which curve around' make it 'difficult to see the stage clearly' from a seated position. Tripadvisor reviewer in top row balcony: 'leg room was painfully limited' (the one spot where the Lyric's generous-legroom reputation breaks down). No T1 source recommends these seats at any price.
